deficits.evidence: No purpose-built sidewalk is present; pedestrians must walk in the road or on dirt edges.
deficits.suggestion: Construct a continuous sidewalk on the left side of the road to separate pedestrians from vehicle traffic.

deficits.evidence: No purpose-built sidewalk is present; the area consists of dirt and construction debris.
deficits.suggestion: Install a paved sidewalk on the right side to provide a safe walking space for pedestrians.

deficits.evidence: There is high crossing demand due to mixed land use and buildings on both sides, but no designated crossing facility exists.
deficits.suggestion: Install a marked pedestrian crossing to provide a safe and visible point for people to cross the road.

ratings.reason: The left side lacks a formal sidewalk, and building one is feasible given the available space.
The right side consists of dirt and debris with no formal footway, making a sidewalk a feasible addition.
No designated crossing is visible despite the urban environment, and installing one is a standard feasible measure.
